desc: Detects specific weeks within a month for intramonth pattern analysis. Research by Fosback (1976) and Ariel (1987) shows stock returns are positive only during the first half of calendar months. The first week benefits from payroll-related capital inflows and turn-of-month overlap (Ogden 1990). The third week contains options expiration (OPEX) effects -- triple witching weeks (March, June, September, December) show 2x normal volume and elevated volatility. The last week shows anticipatory turn-of-month buying.

name: Quarter

options.name: Quarter
options.desc: The specific quarter to detect

desc: Detects specific quarters for quarterly calendar patterns including window dressing by fund managers, pension fund rebalancing, and earnings seasonality. Q4 is historically the strongest quarter, with the S&P 500 averaging +4.4% gains when positive year-to-date through Q3. Research shows approximately $32 billion in quarterly pension rebalancing equity flows occur at quarter-end. However, the quarter-end effect outside of Q4/December is largely unsupported by backtests -- excluding December, quarter-end returns average -0.11% per trade.

name: Month of Year

options.name: Month
options.desc: The specific month to detect

desc: Detects specific months for seasonal calendar patterns documented in decades of academic research. The January effect (Rozeff & Kinney 1976, Keim 1983) shows small-cap stocks outperforming significantly in January, with nearly half the annual size premium concentrated in a single month. 'Sell in May and Go Away' (Bouman & Jacobsen 2002) validated November-April outperformance across 36 of 37 international markets. The Santa Claus rally (Yale Hirsch 1972) covers the last 5 trading days of December plus first 2 of January, occurring 79% of years since 1950 with average S&P 500 returns of +1.3%.

name: Day of Week

options.name: Weekday
options.desc: The specific weekday to detect

desc: Detects specific weekdays for day-of-week calendar effects. The Monday/weekend effect, first documented by Cross (1973) and rigorously studied by French (1980) and Gibbons & Hess (1981), showed significantly negative Monday returns and positive Friday returns in the S&P 500 (1953-1977). A 2024 meta-analysis of 85 studies confirms Mondays/Tuesdays provide lower average daily returns while Wednesdays/Fridays indicate higher returns. However, the effect has largely vanished in US large-cap markets since the 1990s and is now mainly observed in emerging markets and small caps.

name: Kelly

options.name: Fraction
options.desc: Kelly fraction (0.5 = half-Kelly, more conservative)
options.tuningGuidance: 0.5 (half-Kelly, default) achieves ~75% of full Kelly growth rate with ~50% of the volatility. 0.25 (quarter-Kelly) for uncertain or unstable edge. 1.0 (full Kelly) only appropriate with 500+ trades and demonstrably stable edge — extremely aggressive.

options.name: Minimum Trades
options.desc: Minimum trades required before using Kelly (uses fallback_pct until reached)
options.tuningGuidance: 30 (default) minimum for statistical reliability. 50-100 for variable win rates or strategies with fat-tailed returns. Until reached, uses fallback_pct as static allocation.

options.name: Fallback Percent
options.desc: Equity percentage to use when insufficient trade history (10 = 10%)
options.tuningGuidance: 10.0 (default). Should roughly match expected Kelly allocation to avoid a size discontinuity when switching from fallback to Kelly at min_trades threshold.

desc: Kelly Criterion optimal sizing. f* = W - (1-W)/R where W = win rate, R = avg_win/avg_loss. Uses historical trades to estimate edge. Half-Kelly commonly used for stability.

name: Position Size

options.name: Size Type
options.desc: How to interpret size: 'unit' = raw units (shares for stocks, contracts for futures, base currency units for FX — e.g. 100000 = 1 standard lot EURUSD), 'notional' = $ value, 'percent' = % of equity (5 = 5%)
options.tuningGuidance: percent (default) most flexible — scales with equity automatically. unit for fixed-size positions (specific share/contract counts). notional for dollar exposure targets. FX: prefer notional or percent over unit to avoid manual lot math.

desc: Dynamic position sizing. Takes a size input and outputs to fixed 'size' key. Unit meaning varies by asset class: stocks=shares, futures=contracts, FX=base currency units (100000=1 std lot), crypto=base coins. For long/short strategies, use conditional_select to merge weights before this component. Only ONE position_size is allowed per strategy. Use rebalance_on to gate when sizing recalculates (e.g., rebalance_on=is_new_month).

name: Risk Unit

options.name: Risk Mode
options.desc: How to interpret risk_pct: 'percent' = percentage of equity (1 = 1%), 'fixed' = fixed dollar amount (200 = $200 risk per trade)
options.tuningGuidance: percent (default) scales with equity — standard for most strategies. fixed = constant dollar risk regardless of equity. Use fixed for drawdown recovery or income strategies where position size shouldn't shrink with losses.

options.name: Risk/Reward Ratio
options.desc: Risk/reward ratio for take profit. 0 = no take profit (default). Set > 0 to enable automatic TP at rr_ratio * stop_distance from entry (e.g., 2.0 = TP at 2x the stop distance)
options.tuningGuidance: 0 (default) = no TP, exit only via signal or SL. 1.5-2.0 for trend-following (captures moves at 1.5-2x risk). 3.0+ for reversal strategies with low win rate. Match to historical payoff ratio — if avg_win/avg_loss is 2.5, start with rr_ratio=2.0-2.5.

options.name: Minimum Size
options.desc: Minimum position size (0 = no minimum)
options.tuningGuidance: 0 (default) = no minimum. Set to 1 for stocks/futures (whole shares/contracts). Leave 0 for crypto (fractional sizing allowed).

options.name: Maximum Size
options.desc: Maximum position size (0 = no maximum)
options.tuningGuidance: 0 (default) = no max. Set to prevent concentration: max_size = equity * max_allocation_pct / price. For futures, cap at account margin limits.

options.name: Lot Size
options.desc: Round position size to multiples of lot_size. Examples: 1 = whole shares/contracts, 100 = board lots, 0.001 = crypto. 0 = no rounding (fractional allowed)
options.tuningGuidance: 0 (default) = fractional. 1 = whole shares/contracts. 100 = board lots (US equities). FX: 1000 = micro lot, 10000 = mini lot, 100000 = standard lot.

options.name: Size Scalar
options.desc: Multiplier applied to final size. Use 0.5 for half-positions, 2.0 for double.
options.tuningGuidance: 1.0 (default) = no scaling. 0.5 for paper trading or risk reduction. 2.0 for scaling up a validated strategy. Applies after all other size calculations.

options.name: Contract Multiplier Override
options.desc: Override asset.GetMultiplier(). 0 = use asset's multiplier from AssetSpecification (stocks=1, E-mini=50, CL=1000, etc.). Set >0 to override for custom lot sizes.
options.tuningGuidance: 0 (default) = auto-detect from asset specification (E-mini=50, CL=1000, GC=100, stocks=1). Override only for non-standard contracts or synthetic data where the asset spec is missing or incorrect.

options.name: Stop Distance Unit
options.desc: Unit for stop_distance: 'price' = absolute price units (default), 'pips' = FX pips (0.0001 or 0.01 for JPY pairs), 'percent' = percentage of entry price (1 = 1%)
options.tuningGuidance: price (default) for stocks/futures — use with ATR-based stops. pips for FX (auto-detects JPY 0.01 vs standard 0.0001). percent for multi-asset portfolios where you want uniform percentage-based stops across different price levels.

desc: Atomic risk-based sizing that computes position size and stop loss, with optional take profit. By default, position size is computed ONCE at entry and held until the position is closed (stop loss and take profit still update dynamically). To enable periodic resizing, connect a rebalance_on input (e.g., rebalance_on=is_new_week). Supports two risk modes: 'percent' (default) where risk_pct is a percentage of equity (1 = 1%), and 'fixed' where risk_pct is an absolute dollar amount ($200 = risk $200 per trade). Formula (percent): size = (equity * risk_pct/100) / (stop_distance * contract_multiplier) * size_scalar. Formula (fixed): size = risk_pct / (stop_distance * contract_multiplier) * size_scalar. stop_distance can be in price units, pips, or percent (see stop_unit option). contract_multiplier defaults to asset.GetMultiplier() (E-mini=50, CL=1000, stocks=1). SL is always set at stop_distance from entry. TP is opt-in: set rr_ratio > 0 to add TP at rr_ratio * stop_distance, or pass tp_distance input for explicit TP.

name: Take Profit

options.name: Distance Unit
options.desc: How to interpret the distance value
options.tuningGuidance: Same as stop_loss unit. price (default) for stocks/futures. pips for FX. percent for multi-asset portfolios.

options.name: R-Multiple Levels
options.desc: R-multiple levels for tiered exits (e.g., [1, 2, 3]). Must sum to 1.0 with exit_pcts.
options.tuningGuidance: Empty (default) = single level, use distance input. Common setups: [1,2,3] equal spacing, [1,1.5,3] front-loaded, [1,3] runner style. Array length must match exit_pcts length.

options.name: Exit Percentages
options.desc: Exit percentage at each level (e.g., [0.33, 0.33, 0.34]). Must sum to 1.0.
options.tuningGuidance: Must sum to ~1.0. [0.33,0.33,0.34] equal thirds. [0.50,0.30,0.20] front-loaded — takes half off at first target. [0.75,0.25] runner style — secures most at 1R, lets remainder run.

desc: Take profit exit level(s). Supports single level or tiered exits. For tiered: use r_levels and exit_pcts with risk_distance. Long positions: exit at entry + distance. Short positions: exit at entry - distance.

name: Stop Loss

options.name: Distance Unit
options.desc: How to interpret the distance value
options.tuningGuidance: price (default) for stocks/futures — use with ATR-based stops. pips for FX (auto-detects JPY 0.01 vs standard 0.0001). percent for multi-asset portfolios with uniform stop rules.

desc: Stop loss exit level. Sets exit at a fixed distance from entry. Long positions: exit at entry - distance. Short positions: exit at entry + distance.

name: Multi-Linear Fit (Multi-Factor Regression)

options.name: Number of Independent Variables
options.desc: Number of independent variables (regressors) in the model
options.tuningGuidance: Set to match your factor model: 1 for CAPM, 3 for Fama-French 3-factor, 5 for Fama-French 5-factor. More factors increase model complexity and risk of overfitting.

options.name: Window Size
options.desc: Rolling window size for OLS regression
options.tuningGuidance: Use 60-120 for stable factor exposure estimates (matches academic practice). Shorter windows (20-40) for tactical factor timing. Minimum observation count should exceed number of factors by at least 10x for reliable estimates.

desc: Multi-variate OLS regression: y = β₀ + β₁x₁ + β₂x₂ + ... + βₙxₙ + ε. Computes factor exposures (betas), intercept (alpha), residuals (idiosyncratic returns), and R-squared. Essential for Fama-French factor regressions and multi-factor models.

name: Z-Score

options.name: Window
options.desc: Rolling window size for calculating mean and standard deviation
options.tuningGuidance: Shorter windows (10-15) for responsive mean-reversion entries, captures recent regime quickly but noisier. Standard 20 balances stability with adaptation. Longer windows (40-60) for stable normalization in ML features or cross-asset comparisons. Match window to your mean-reversion timeframe.

desc: Rolling z-score of the input series: (x_t - mean)/stddev over the configured window.

name: Volatility Estimator

options.name: Estimator Type
options.desc: Volatility estimation method to use
options.tuningGuidance: garman_klass: Best general-purpose, ~8x more efficient than close-to-close, uses full OHLC. parkinson: High-low range only, ~5x efficient, good when open/close unavailable. yang_zhang: Best for markets with overnight gaps (stocks), combines overnight and intraday components. hodges_tompkins: Bias-corrected for small samples, close-to-close only.

options.name: Period
options.desc: Lookback window for volatility calculation
options.tuningGuidance: Shorter periods (7-10) track volatility changes quickly but are noisier. Standard 14-21 for tactical trading. Longer periods (30-60) for strategic allocation. For options pricing, match to the target expiration horizon.

options.name: Trading Periods Per Year
options.desc: Annual trading period count for annualizing volatility
options.tuningGuidance: Use 252 for US stocks, 365 for crypto (24/7 markets), ~260 for international equities. For hourly data, use 252*6.5 (~1638). For 5-min data, 252*6.5*12 (~19656).

desc: Range-based volatility estimators that are more efficient than close-to-close standard deviation. Garman-Klass (1980) and Yang-Zhang (2000) use full OHLC data. Parkinson (1980) uses high-low range. Hodges-Tompkins (2002) provides bias-corrected estimates for small samples using close-to-close returns.

name: Fractional Differentiation (FFD)

options.name: Differentiation Order
options.desc: Fractional differentiation order. Values between 0 and 1 balance stationarity and memory preservation.
options.tuningGuidance: Start with d=0.5 and test stationarity with rolling_adf. If not stationary, increase d. The goal is the MINIMUM d that achieves stationarity (p < 0.05 on ADF test). Typical range: 0.3-0.7 for most financial series. d=1.0 equals standard differencing (full memory loss). d < 0.3 rarely achieves stationarity. d > 1.0 is over-differencing.

options.name: Weight Threshold
options.desc: Minimum weight threshold. Weights below this are truncated, determining the effective window size.
options.tuningGuidance: Default 1e-5 works well. Lower thresholds (1e-8) use more history (longer effective window) for higher fidelity but more NaN warm-up. Higher thresholds (1e-3) truncate more aggressively for faster computation and less warm-up.

desc: Fixed-Width Window Fractional Differentiation (FFD). Transforms a time series to achieve stationarity while preserving maximum memory/predictive information. Unlike integer differencing (d=1) which removes all memory, fractional differencing with d < 1 maintains a controlled amount of historical information. Based on Lopez de Prado's 'Advances in Financial Machine Learning' (2018), Chapter 5.

name: Engle-Granger Cointegration

options.name: Window Size
options.desc: Rolling window size for cointegration test. Minimum 100 recommended.
options.tuningGuidance: Use 100-250 for stable hedge ratios on daily data. Shorter windows (60-100) for more adaptive but noisier hedge ratios. Match to expected regime duration. Too short = noisy hedge ratio, too long = stale hedge ratio.

options.name: ADF Lags
options.desc: Number of lags for ADF test on residuals (default 1).

options.name: Significance Level
options.desc: Significance level for is_cointegrated output (default 0.05).

desc: Two-step Engle-Granger cointegration test (1987 Nobel Prize methodology). Step 1: Regress Y on X via OLS to get hedge ratio (beta) and intercept (alpha). Step 2: Test residuals (Y - alpha - beta*X) for stationarity using ADF. If residuals are stationary, the series are cointegrated - their linear combination is mean-reverting even if individual series are non-stationary.

name: Long & Short Zone

options.name: Hold Long
options.desc: Duration to hold long position after entry. 0 = no hold, 20 = 20 bars, 20D = 20 days.
options.tuningGuidance: 0 (default) = signal-driven exit. 5-20 bars for momentum/PEAD. 5D-20D for calendar holds. Longer holds reduce turnover but increase drawdown risk.

options.name: Hold Short
options.desc: Duration to hold short position after entry. 0 = no hold, 20 = 20 bars, 20D = 20 days.
options.tuningGuidance: Typically match hold_long unless asymmetric conviction (e.g., faster short exits in trending markets).

options.name: Strict Hold
options.desc: When true, opposing signals are ignored during hold period. Position only exits when hold expires or TP/SL triggers. When false (default), opposing signals override current hold.
options.tuningGuidance: false (default) = opposing signals flip position immediately. true = locked during hold. Use true with risk_unit SL/TP for clean exit management.

desc: Consolidated zone executor for long/short signals with hold options. Outputs signal column: 0=close, 1=long, -1=short. By default, opposing signals override hold. Use strict_hold=True to ignore opposing signals during hold.

name: Half-Life AR(1)

options.name: Window Size
options.desc: Rolling window size for half-life calculation. Minimum 20 recommended for statistical validity.
options.tuningGuidance: Use 50-100 for stable half-life estimates on daily data. Shorter windows (20-30) capture recent regime changes but are noisier. Longer windows (200+) for strategic pair evaluation. Window should be at least 10x the expected half-life.

desc: Estimate mean-reversion half-life using AR(1) model. Fits y(t) = alpha + beta*y(t-1) + epsilon, then computes half_life = -ln(2)/ln(beta). Used in pairs trading to estimate how quickly a spread reverts to mean. Lower half-life indicates faster mean reversion.

name: Pivot Point Support & Resistance
desc: Classic floor trader pivot points with three levels of support (S1-S3) and resistance (R1-R3). Calculated from previous bar's high, low, and close. Pivot = (H+L+C)/3, then support and resistance levels are derived from the pivot, high, and low.

name: Rolling Hurst Exponent

options.name: Window Size
options.desc: Rolling window size for Hurst exponent calculation
options.tuningGuidance: Use 50-100 for tactical regime detection (responds faster to regime shifts). Use 200-500 for strategic classification (more stable). Lag grid is automatically scaled to window size. Minimum 20 for any meaningful estimate.

desc: Rolling-window Hurst exponent using rescaled range (R/S) analysis. Computes H over a fixed rolling window to detect time-varying regime changes. H < 0.5 = mean-reverting, H = 0.5 = random walk, H > 0.5 = trending. Lag grid automatically adapts to window size.

name: Vortex Indicator

options.name: Period
options.desc: Lookback period for Vortex Indicator calculation
options.tuningGuidance: Standard 14. Shorter periods (7-10) for faster but noisier signals. Longer periods (21-30) for smoother trend identification. Use 14 for daily charts as a good balance.

desc: Two-line trend indicator (VI+ and VI-) based on the concept of positive and negative trend movements. Introduced by Etienne Botes and Douglas Siepman (2010), inspired by Viktor Schauberger's vortex flow analysis. VI+ measures upward trend strength, VI- measures downward trend strength.

name: Rollover Policy
desc: Provides front contract info for futures rollover detection. Connect the active input to a futures_continuation.s output. At runtime, the execution engine reads the current front contract and compares with held positions to detect rollovers.

name: Gauge Chart - ONE PER ASSET

options.name: Chart Title
options.desc: Title for the gauge chart
options.tuningGuidance: Describe what metric is displayed.

options.name: Category
options.desc: Category for grouping in dashboard
options.tuningGuidance: Required.

options.name: Aggregation
options.desc: Aggregation function to apply to the input series before display
options.tuningGuidance: Default Last. Use Mean for averaged readings.

options.name: Minimum Value
options.desc: Minimum value for the gauge. For categorical gauges, defines the lower bound of the input range for auto-scaling to categories.
options.tuningGuidance: Default 0. Set to match the input data range.

options.name: Maximum Value
options.desc: Maximum value for the gauge. For categorical gauges, defines the upper bound of the input range for auto-scaling to categories.
options.tuningGuidance: Default 100. Set to match the input data range.

options.name: Value Type
options.desc: Format type for the value (Decimal, Percent, Monetary, Integer)
options.tuningGuidance: Default DecimalFormat.

options.name: Decimal Places
options.desc: Number of decimal places to display (default: 2)
options.tuningGuidance: Use 0 for whole numbers, 2 for decimals.

options.name: Solid Gauge
options.desc: Use solid gauge (true) or dial gauge (false)
options.tuningGuidance: Default true (solid). Solid gauge fills an arc, dial shows a needle.

options.name: Gauge Color
options.desc: Color for the gauge (ignored if using traffic light colors)
options.tuningGuidance: Choose from palette. Default uses theme color.

options.name: Traffic Light Colors
options.desc: Use red-yellow-green color scheme
options.tuningGuidance: Enable for metrics where green=good, red=bad.

options.name: Categories
options.desc: Category labels for categorical gauge (e.g., ['Extreme Fear', 'Fear', 'Neutral', 'Greed', 'Extreme Greed']). When set, the input value is auto-scaled from [min, max] to [0, N] where N is the category count. For example, with RSI (0-100) and 5 categories, set min=0, max=100 and the gauge maps RSI to the appropriate category.
options.tuningGuidance: Use for sentiment indices. Define categories from worst to best. Set min/max to match the input scale.

options.name: Display Order
options.desc: Display order within dashboard category (lower values appear first, 0 = default position)

desc: Single-value gauge display for KPIs and metrics. One gauge per asset.

name: Rolling ADF Test

options.name: Window Size
options.desc: Rolling window size for ADF test. Minimum 50 recommended for reliable results.
options.tuningGuidance: Use 100-200 for reliable p-values on daily data. Minimum 50 for any meaningful result. Shorter windows track stationarity changes faster but give less reliable statistics. Match to your trading horizon.

options.name: ADF Lags
options.desc: Number of lags for ADF regression (default 1).
options.tuningGuidance: Default 1 is sufficient for most applications. Use higher lags (2-4) for series with strong autocorrelation. Too many lags reduce test power.

options.name: Significance Level
options.desc: Significance level for is_stationary output (default 0.05, options: 0.01, 0.05, 0.10).

options.name: Deterministic Terms
options.desc: Deterministic terms: 'nc' (no constant), 'c' (constant only, default), 'ct' (constant + trend).
options.tuningGuidance: Use 'c' for spreads and residuals (most common). Use 'ct' if the series has a deterministic trend component. Use 'nc' for already-demeaned series.

desc: Rolling Augmented Dickey-Fuller test for stationarity. Tests null hypothesis that series has a unit root (non-stationary). Returns test statistic, p-value, and critical values at 1%, 5%, 10% significance. Uses MacKinnon (1994, 2010) tables for p-value computation.

name: Williams %R
desc: Williams %R. Momentum oscillator that indicates overbought/oversold conditions relative to high-low range.

name: Weighted Close Price
desc: Weighted Close Price. Average of OHLC prices with extra weight given to close: (H+L+C+C)/4.

name: Volume Oscillator
desc: Volume Oscillator. Shows difference between two volume moving averages as percentage, indicating volume trends.

name: Trix
desc: Trix. Triple exponentially smoothed moving average oscillator, showing percentage rate of change.

name: True Range
desc: True Range. Measures market volatility by comparing current price range to previous close.

name: Stochastic RSI
desc: Stochastic RSI. Applies stochastic formula to RSI values, creating a more sensitive oscillator.

name: Stochastic Oscillator
desc: Stochastic Oscillator. Compares closing price to price range over a period, indicating momentum and overbought/oversold conditions.

name: Standard Error Over Period
desc: Standard Error Over Period. Calculates the standard error over the specified period.

name: Acceleration Bands

options.name: Period
options.desc: SMA period for the middle band and band width calculation
options.tuningGuidance: Standard 20 for daily charts. Shorter periods (10-15) for intraday or more responsive bands. Longer periods (30-50) for strategic volatility analysis.

options.name: Width Multiplier
options.desc: Multiplier for band width based on high-low range percentage
options.tuningGuidance: Default 4.0. Higher values widen bands (fewer breakout signals, more conservative). Lower values (2.0-3.0) for tighter, more responsive bands.

desc: Volatility envelope based on the high-low range as a percentage of the typical price. Upper and lower bands expand and contract with market volatility, providing adaptive breakout and overbought/oversold levels. Middle band is a simple moving average.

name: Accumulation/Distribution Line
desc: Accumulation/Distribution Line. Volume-based indicator designed to measure cumulative flow of money into and out of a security.

name: Cross-Sectional Momentum

options.name: Group By
options.desc: Group assets before applying cross-sectional operation. When set, the transform operates within each group independently.
options.tuningGuidance: Use 'sector' for industry-neutral stock strategies. Use 'category' for futures. Use 'auto_detect' to let the system choose.

desc: Computes cumulative cross-sectional mean returns across all assets at each timestamp. Calculates the average percentage change across the universe, then compounds it into a cumulative index representing aggregate market momentum.

name: Trailing Stop

options.name: Step Size
options.desc: Discrete step size for trailing (0 = continuous)
options.tuningGuidance: 0 (default) = continuous trailing, updates every bar. Best for trending markets. 0.25-1.0 for stocks — reduces whipsaw in choppy markets by requiring meaningful moves before adjusting. Larger steps for more volatile assets.

desc: Trailing stop that follows price. Activates after reaching activation_distance profit, then trails at distance from highest (long) or lowest (short) price.

name: Ulcer Index

options.name: Period
options.desc: Lookback window for measuring drawdown severity
options.tuningGuidance: Standard 14 for short-term pain measurement. Use 21-30 for typical drawdown analysis. Longer periods (60+) for strategic risk assessment. Martin (1987) originally used 14 for mutual fund evaluation.

options.name: Use Sum
options.desc: If true, returns the sum of squared drawdowns instead of the RMS (root mean square). The standard Ulcer Index uses RMS (false). Sum variant useful for cumulative pain measurement.

desc: Downside volatility measure that focuses on drawdowns from rolling peaks rather than overall volatility. Developed by Peter Martin (1987). Also known as the 'pain index'. Measures the root mean square of percentage drawdowns from the highest value in the window.

name: Balance Sheet

options.name: Reporting Period
options.desc: Reporting period: quarterly (10-Q) or annual (10-K). TTM is not available for balance sheets (point-in-time snapshot, not a flow).

desc: Load balance sheet fundamental data. Provides assets, liabilities, equity, and other balance sheet metrics over time.

name: Swing Highs and Lows

options.name: Swing Length
options.desc: Number of bars on each side required to confirm swing point
options.tuningGuidance: 3-5 for scalping/intraday (more sensitive). 5-10 for swing trading (balanced). 10-20 for position trading (major swings only). Higher values reduce noise but increase lag.

desc: Identifies swing high and low points in price data by finding local peaks and valleys within a specified lookback period.

name: Cross-Sectional Factor Analysis

options.name: Correlation Method
options.desc: Type of correlation for IC calculation
options.tuningGuidance: Spearman (default): robust to outliers, captures monotonic relationships. Pearson: linear relationships, sensitive to outliers. Kendall: most robust, but computationally expensive.

options.name: Minimum Observations
options.desc: Minimum valid observations required per timestamp
options.tuningGuidance: Use 10+ for stable IC estimates. Increase for smaller universes with potential missing data.

options.name: IR Window
options.desc: Rolling window for Information Ratio calculation
options.tuningGuidance: 252 (1 year) is standard for annualized IR. Use 63 (quarterly) for faster adaptation.

desc: Computes Information Coefficient (IC) and related statistics for factor research. Correlates a factor signal with forward returns ACROSS assets at each timestamp, returning time series of IC, t-statistic, p-value, and Information Ratio.

name: Psychological Support Levels (PSL)

options.name: Period
options.desc: Lookback window for computing the percentage of bars closing above the open
options.tuningGuidance: Use 10-20 for responsive sentiment readings. Standard 12 captures ~2 weeks of daily data. Longer periods (30-60) for stable market sentiment assessment.

desc: Measures the percentage of bars in the lookback window where the close exceeded the open. Acts as a market sentiment oscillator: values above 50% indicate bullish sentiment (more up-closes than down-closes), below 50% bearish. Based on psychological market behavior patterns.

name: Financial Ratio

options.name: Ratio Type
options.desc: Select the financial ratio to calculate

options.name: Reporting Period
options.desc: Financial statement reporting period for underlying data

desc: Calculates financial ratios from fundamental data using vectorized operations. Valuation ratios (P/B, B/M, P/S) correctly use market cap (price × shares) per academic standards (Fama-French 1992).

name: CUSUM Change Point Detector

options.name: Threshold
options.desc: Amplitude threshold for detecting a change (used if use_std_threshold=false)
options.tuningGuidance: Higher = fewer but more significant detections. Start with 4-6x expected noise level.

options.name: Drift
options.desc: Drift term to prevent false alarms in stable periods
options.tuningGuidance: Use 0 for sensitive detection, 0.5-1.0x noise level for robustness.

options.name: Use Std-Based Threshold
options.desc: If true, threshold = std_multiplier * std(differences)

options.name: Std Multiplier
options.desc: Number of standard deviations for threshold (when use_std_threshold=true)
options.tuningGuidance: 3-4 for sensitive, 5-6 for conservative. Like a z-score threshold.

desc: CUSUM (Cumulative Sum) change-point detection algorithm (Page 1954). Detects abrupt mean shifts and structural breaks in time series by tracking cumulative deviations. Signals when accumulated drift exceeds threshold. Detects both upward and downward regime changes.

name: Session Window

options.name: Aggregation Per Extra Input
options.desc: List of AggregationType values for extra inputs. Not needed for OHLC (fixed: First, Max, Min, Last).

desc: Computes OHLCV statistics for defined session windows using predefined sessions (NewYork, London, Tokyo), custom time ranges, or session deltas. Captures intraday market microstructure patterns including the U-shaped volume curve (Admati & Pfleiderer 1988), overnight drift (NY Fed research shows 60%+ of equity returns accrue overnight), and event-driven volatility (NFP releases create 50-100 bps moves). SessionDelta enables precise windows like 'first 30 minutes of NY session' for studying opening reversals, closing auction dynamics, or macro data release reactions.

name: Directional Movement Index
desc: Directional Movement Index. Measures trending strength by comparing +DI and -DI indicators.

name: Pie Chart - ONE PER ASSET

options.name: Chart Title
options.desc: Title for the pie chart
options.tuningGuidance: Describe what composition is shown.

options.name: Inner Size (Donut)
options.desc: Inner cutout percentage (0 = pie, 50+ = donut)
options.tuningGuidance: Use 0 for pie, 50-70 for donut style.

options.name: Slice Colors
options.desc: Colors for each pie slice (e.g., Red, Blue, Green)
options.tuningGuidance: Assign colors matching category meaning.

options.name: Display Order
options.desc: Display order within dashboard category (lower values appear first, 0 = default position)

desc: Pie/donut chart showing proportional composition from label and value columns. Groups by label, sums values per group, normalizes as percentage of total. Set inner_size > 0 (typically 50-70) for donut style. Use for portfolio allocation, sector breakdown, win/loss composition with 2-8 categories.

name: Futures Continuation

options.name: Rollover Method
options.desc: Method for detecting when to roll from front to back contract. FirstOfMonth rolls on the 1st trading day of the expiry month. LastTradingDay rolls N days before the last trading day. LiquidityBased rolls when back contract volume exceeds front.
options.tuningGuidance: FirstOfMonth is the most common. Use LastTradingDay with an offset for contracts that lose liquidity before expiry. LiquidityBased is data-adaptive but requires volume data.

options.name: Adjustment Method
options.desc: Price adjustment method to eliminate gaps between contracts. NoAdjustment passes raw prices through without adjustment. BackwardPanamaCanal adjusts historical prices by absolute difference. BackwardRatio adjusts by ratio (preserves returns). Forward variants adjust future prices instead of historical.
options.tuningGuidance: BackwardPanamaCanal is standard for most strategies. Use BackwardRatio when percentage returns matter more than levels. Forward methods are less common but avoid changing historical data. NoAdjustment for raw unadjusted continuation.

options.name: Roll Offset Days
options.desc: Number of days offset for rollover. For LastTradingDay, rolls N days before the last trading day. For FirstOfMonth, shifts the roll date.
options.tuningGuidance: 0 is standard. Increase to 1-5 for illiquid contracts that need earlier rolls to avoid slippage.

options.name: Spread Depth
options.desc: Compute calendar spread between front month and the Nth deferred contract. 0 = disabled (no spread output). 1 = front vs 2nd nearby, 2 = front vs 3rd nearby, etc. Spread = front.close - deferred.close (positive = backwardation, negative = contango). Use AdjustmentType.NoAdjustment for meaningful spread values.
options.tuningGuidance: 2 is the most common (front vs 3rd nearby). Use 1 for near-term tightness, 11 for full curve slope. NaN when deferred contract is unavailable.

desc: Builds continuous futures price series from individual contracts. Detects rollover dates using the specified rollover method and applies price adjustments to eliminate gaps between contracts.

name: String Contains

options.name: Operation
options.desc: Type of containment check

options.name: Pattern
options.desc: Pattern to search for

desc: Check if strings contain, start with, or end with a pattern. Returns boolean.

name: Qstick
desc: Qstick. Measures the ratio of black to white candlesticks, indicating buying and selling pressure.

name: ArgMax (Timestamp)

options.name: Expanding Mode
options.desc: If true, returns expanding argmax (timestamp of max seen so far at each point). If false, returns global argmax timestamp for all rows.
options.tuningGuidance: true (default) = expanding mode: at each row, returns the timestamp of the maximum value seen from the start up to that row. Tracks when the current peak was established. false = global mode: returns the same timestamp for every row — the date of the overall series maximum. Useful for labeling the best day across an entire backtest.

desc: Returns the timestamp where the maximum value occurred. In expanding mode, tracks the running maximum's timestamp at each point. In global mode, broadcasts the single global argmax timestamp to all rows.

name: Typical Price
desc: Typical Price. Average of high, low, and close prices for each period, representing a balanced price.

name: Keyword Match

options.name: Keywords
options.desc: List of keyword patterns to detect in text. 'patterns': array of strings (plain substrings or regex). 'case_sensitive': false by default (case-insensitive matching). 'use_regex': false by default (plain substring search). Example: {patterns: ["upgrade", "downgrade"], case_sensitive: false, use_regex: false}. With use_regex=true: {patterns: ["fraud|embezzle", "sec.+investigation"]}

desc: Check if ANY keyword pattern matches in text. Returns boolean (true/false). Use for signal generation from news, filtering by keywords, detecting specific events in text data. Academic: Tetlock (2007) shows media pessimism predicts downward price pressure; Loughran & McDonald (2011) demonstrate domain-specific lexicons outperform generic dictionaries by 73.8% in financial text classification. Empirical IC: ~0.08 when used with bullish/bearish keyword lists on news headlines.

name: Streak Length

options.name: Direction
options.desc: Which direction to count streaks
options.tuningGuidance: up = consecutive true, down = consecutive false, bidirectional = positive for true/negative for false

desc: Counts consecutive occurrences of true/false values in a boolean series. Returns running count that resets when condition changes.

name: Average True Range
desc: Average True Range. Measures market volatility by calculating the average range between price points.

name: Hierarchical Risk Parity

options.name: Linkage Method
options.desc: Clustering linkage method: single, complete, average, ward
options.tuningGuidance: single (default) produces chaining — long thin clusters. ward minimizes within-cluster variance and typically gives more balanced clusters. complete tends to produce compact clusters. average is a compromise. ward is often preferred for portfolio construction.

options.name: Lookback Period
options.desc: Number of periods for covariance estimation
options.tuningGuidance: 252 (default, ~1 year daily). Shorter (60-126) adapts faster but may produce unstable cluster structures. Longer (504) for more stable hierarchies. Must exceed number of assets.

options.name: Rebalance Frequency
options.desc: Number of periods between rebalancing (21 = monthly for daily data)
options.tuningGuidance: 21 (default, monthly). HRP is relatively stable between rebalances due to hierarchical structure. 63 (quarterly) often sufficient and reduces turnover.

options.name: Window Type
options.desc: Rolling (fixed-size sliding) or Expanding (cumulative)
options.tuningGuidance: rolling (default) adapts to recent correlation structure. expanding uses all available history — better when correlation structure is believed stable.

options.name: Maximum Weight
options.desc: Maximum weight per asset (caps individual weights)
options.tuningGuidance: 1.0 (default) imposes no cap. Set to 0.20-0.40 for large universes to prevent concentration. HRP naturally diversifies, so caps are less critical than for mean-variance methods.

desc: Hierarchical Risk Parity uses hierarchical clustering to group correlated assets, then allocates weights through recursive bisection inversely proportional to cluster variance. Uses rolling estimation with configurable rebalance frequency. Reference: Lopez de Prado (2016). Does not require matrix inversion.

name: VWAP
desc: Volume Weighted Average Price per bar (provider 'vw').

name: Maximum Diversification

options.name: Lookback Period
options.desc: Number of periods for covariance estimation
options.tuningGuidance: 252 (default, ~1 year daily). Shorter (60-126) adapts faster to changing correlations. Longer (504) for more stable diversification ratios. Must exceed number of assets.

options.name: Rebalance Frequency
options.desc: Number of periods between rebalancing (21 = monthly for daily data)
options.tuningGuidance: 21 (default, monthly). Diversification ratio is driven by correlations which change slowly. 63 (quarterly) often sufficient and reduces turnover.

options.name: Window Type
options.desc: Rolling (fixed-size sliding) or Expanding (cumulative)
options.tuningGuidance: rolling (default) adapts to recent correlation structure. expanding uses all data — useful when long-term correlation structure is the target.

options.name: Maximum Weight
options.desc: Maximum weight per asset
options.tuningGuidance: 1.0 (default) imposes no cap. The optimizer may concentrate in assets with unique (low-correlation) risk profiles. Set to 0.20-0.40 for balanced portfolios.

desc: Maximum Diversification portfolio maximizes the diversification ratio DR = (w'σ)/σ_p where σ is individual volatilities and σ_p is portfolio volatility. Exploits correlation benefits without requiring return estimates.

name: Keyword Score

options.name: Keywords
options.desc: List of weighted keyword patterns. Each entry has 'pattern' (string) and 'weight' (double). Score = sum(count_i * weight_i) for each pattern. 'case_sensitive': false by default. 'use_regex': false by default. Example: {keywords: [{pattern: "fraud", weight: 5.0}, {pattern: "lawsuit", weight: 2.0}]}. Use positive weights for bullish terms, negative for bearish, or severity-based scaling.

desc: Compute weighted score from keyword pattern matches. Returns decimal (double). Each pattern has a weight; score = sum of (count * weight) across all patterns. Use for custom sentiment scoring with severity weights. Academic: Loughran-McDonald (2011) 6 sentiment categories; Jegadeesh & Wu (2013) 'Word Power' term-weighting; Garcia (2013) shows sentiment during recessions has stronger predictive power. Empirical: Risk keyword scores show IC ~-0.11 (high risk predicts poor returns); dictionary IC ~0.08-0.13 (declining with crowding); FinBERT 88.2% vs LM dictionary 62.1% accuracy.

name: Chande Momentum Oscillator
desc: Chande Momentum Oscillator. Momentum oscillator calculating relative momentum of positive and negative price movements.

name: Session Gap

options.name: Fill Percentage
options.desc: Minimum fill percentage for gap_filled signal
options.tuningGuidance: 100% (default) for complete fill. 50-80% for partial fill strategies.

desc: Detects opening gaps between trading sessions (overnight gaps, weekend gaps) and tracks gap-fill behavior. A gap occurs when the current session opens above (gap up) or below (gap down) the prior session's close.

name: SVR L2

options.name: Regularization (C)
options.desc: Inverse of regularization strength

options.name: Epsilon
options.desc: Tolerance for stopping criterion

options.name: Window Size
options.desc: Size of training window (for rolling) or minimum window (for expanding)
options.tuningGuidance: 252 (default): ~1 year of daily data. Use 126 (~6 months) for faster adaptation to regime changes but less training data. Use 504 (~2 years) for more stable models at the cost of slower adaptation. Rule of thumb: window should contain at least 10x the number of features. For intraday bars, scale proportionally.

options.name: Retrain Frequency
options.desc: How often to retrain: 21 = 21 bars, 1M = monthly, 1Y = yearly, 1W = weekly
options.tuningGuidance: 21 (default): Retrain monthly on daily data. Use 1 for every-bar retraining (expensive but most adaptive). Use 63 (quarterly) for slow-changing models. Duration syntax: '1M' = calendar month, '1W' = week, '21' = 21 bars. More frequent retraining = higher computational cost but faster adaptation.

options.name: Window Type
options.desc: Rolling uses fixed-size window; Expanding grows from start
options.tuningGuidance: rolling (default): Fixed-size training window that slides forward. Model sees only recent data, adapts to regime changes, but forgets old patterns. expanding: Training window grows from start (GKX 2020 methodology). Model sees all historical data, more stable but slower to adapt. Use expanding for long-term factor models; rolling for tactical/short-horizon strategies.

options.name: Min Training Samples
options.desc: Minimum samples required before first prediction
options.tuningGuidance: 100 (default): Reasonable minimum for most models. For LightGBM, use 200+ for stable tree construction. For logistic regression, 50 may suffice. Rule of thumb: min_training_samples >= 10 * num_features. Lower values start predictions sooner but risk unreliable early predictions.

desc: L2-regularized support vector regression with rolling/expanding window training. Provides stable return prediction that adapts to changing market conditions.

options.tuningGuidance: NxN grows quickly — keep under 15 for readability.

desc: Cross-sectional color-coded grid across assets. TWO MODES: 'correlation' computes an NxN pairwise correlation matrix between all assets (the standard portfolio diversification diagnostic). 'values' shows a 1xN aggregated metric grid where each asset gets one color-coded cell (visual ranking by color intensity).

name: Earnings
desc: Earnings announcements including EPS, revenue, and surprises. Access actual vs estimated figures, fiscal periods, and earnings importance ratings.

name: Cross-Sectional Rank Quantile

options.name: Ascending
options.desc: If true, lowest value gets 0.0, highest gets 1.0

desc: Assigns percentile ranks (0.0 to 1.0) to assets at each timestamp. Normalizes ordinal ranks to a uniform [0,1] scale for combining factors with different universe sizes.

name: Topic Classify

options.name: Topics
options.desc: Topic dictionary with topic names and associated keyword patterns. 'topics': array of {name: string, patterns: string[]}. 'default_topic': fallback topic when no patterns match (empty string → null). 'case_sensitive': false by default. 'use_regex': false by default. Tie-breaking: when topics have equal match counts, first topic in list wins. Example: {topics: [{name: "earnings", patterns: ["eps", "revenue"]}, {name: "legal", patterns: ["lawsuit", "litigation"]}], default_topic: "other"}

desc: Classify text into topics using dictionary-based matching. Returns topic name (string). Topic with highest keyword match count wins. Use for news categorization, event type detection, content routing. Academic: Garcia (2013) shows topic-specific sentiment drives returns with 10-day response horizon; theme-based sentiment alphas outperform aggregate sentiment. Advantages vs ML: interpretable, deterministic, no training data, fast, audit-friendly.

name: Equal Weight

options.name: Maximum Weight
options.desc: Maximum weight per asset (caps individual weights)
options.tuningGuidance: 1.0 (default) imposes no cap. For diversification, set to 1/N or slightly above (e.g., 0.20 for 5+ assets). Lower values force redistribution of excess weight to other assets.

desc: Cross-sectional allocator that assigns equal weights (1/N) to active assets. Inactive assets (where mask is false) get weight 0. Weights are always unsigned (0 to 1) - direction comes from trade signals.

name: Risk Budgeting

options.name: Lookback Period
options.desc: Number of periods for covariance estimation
options.tuningGuidance: 252 (default, ~1 year daily). Shorter (60-126) reacts faster to regime changes but noisier. Longer (504) for more stable estimates. Must exceed number of assets.

options.name: Rebalance Frequency
options.desc: Number of periods between rebalancing (21 = monthly for daily data)
options.tuningGuidance: 21 (default, monthly). 5 (weekly) for tactical strategies. 63 (quarterly) for lower turnover. Shorter step_size increases turnover and transaction costs.

options.name: Window Type
options.desc: Rolling (fixed-size sliding) or Expanding (cumulative)
options.tuningGuidance: rolling (default) adapts to recent conditions. expanding uses all available history. Use rolling when regime changes matter.

options.name: Maximum Weight
options.desc: Maximum weight per asset
options.tuningGuidance: 1.0 (default) imposes no cap. Tight caps may conflict with budget targets — the optimizer finds the closest feasible allocation. Set to 0.30-0.50 for diversified portfolios.

desc: Risk Budgeting allocates portfolio risk according to specified budget proportions. Each asset's risk contribution equals its budget fraction. Risk Parity is the special case with equal budgets. Use conditional_select with is_asset_ref to specify per-asset budgets.

name: Is Period Boundary

options.name: Period Type
options.desc: Calendar period for boundary detection. week: 7-day cycles (ISO Mon-Sun). month: calendar month transitions. quarter: 3-month blocks (Q1=Jan-Mar, etc.). year: calendar year transitions.

options.name: Boundary Type
options.desc: start: first bar of the new period (safe, no look-ahead). end: last bar of the current period (requires look-ahead to next bar to confirm the period changed).

options.name: Occurrence
options.desc: Which occurrence of the day anchor within the period. first/second/third/fourth/last. Combine with day_anchor for patterns like third Friday (OPEX). none = match any occurrence.

options.name: Day Anchor
options.desc: Weekday to anchor the boundary to. Combine with ordinal for nth-weekday patterns (e.g., ordinal=third, day_anchor=friday for OPEX). none = no weekday filter.

options.name: Day of Month
options.desc: Specific calendar day (1-31) for boundary. 0 = disabled. Values beyond month length snap to last day (e.g., 31 in February → 28/29). Snaps to nearest trading bar.

options.name: Month in Period
options.desc: Which month within the period. For quarter: 1-3 (1=first, 3=last month). For year: 1-12 (1=January, 12=December). 0 = disabled. Use with ordinal+day_anchor for patterns like OPEX (quarter, month_anchor=3, ordinal=third, day_anchor=friday) or Election Day (year, month_anchor=11, ordinal=second, day_anchor=tuesday).

options.name: Bar Offset
options.desc: Shift the boundary signal by N bars. -1 = T-1 pre-positioning (execute one bar before boundary). +1 = T+1 post-settlement (execute one bar after). Commonly used: -1 for pre-rebalance, +1 for post-settlement.

options.name: Timezone
options.desc: IANA timezone for boundary calculation. Determines when a 'day' starts and ends. Critical for intraday bars: 'America/New_York' ensures month boundaries align with US trading sessions, not UTC midnight.

desc: Detect period boundaries (start or end of week, month, quarter, year). Returns a boolean signal: true on bars that mark period transitions. Supports day anchoring (first Monday, last Friday), specific day-of-month, and bar offsets for T-1/T+1 pre/post-positioning patterns.

name: ML Z-Score

options.name: Window Size
options.desc: Size of training window (for rolling) or minimum window (for expanding)
options.tuningGuidance: 252 (default): ~1 year of daily data. Use 126 (~6 months) for faster adaptation to regime changes but less training data. Use 504 (~2 years) for more stable models at the cost of slower adaptation. Rule of thumb: window should contain at least 10x the number of features. For intraday bars, scale proportionally.

options.name: Retrain Frequency
options.desc: How often to retrain: 21 = 21 bars, 1M = monthly, 1Y = yearly, 1W = weekly
options.tuningGuidance: 21 (default): Retrain monthly on daily data. Use 1 for every-bar retraining (expensive but most adaptive). Use 63 (quarterly) for slow-changing models. Duration syntax: '1M' = calendar month, '1W' = week, '21' = 21 bars. More frequent retraining = higher computational cost but faster adaptation.

options.name: Window Type
options.desc: Rolling uses fixed-size window; Expanding grows from start
options.tuningGuidance: rolling (default): Fixed-size training window that slides forward. Model sees only recent data, adapts to regime changes, but forgets old patterns. expanding: Training window grows from start (GKX 2020 methodology). Model sees all historical data, more stable but slower to adapt. Use expanding for long-term factor models; rolling for tactical/short-horizon strategies.

options.name: Min Training Samples
options.desc: Minimum samples required before first prediction
options.tuningGuidance: 100 (default): Reasonable minimum for most models. For LightGBM, use 200+ for stable tree construction. For logistic regression, 50 may suffice. Rule of thumb: min_training_samples >= 10 * num_features. Lower values start predictions sooner but risk unreliable early predictions.

desc: Z-score normalization with rolling/expanding window training. Computes mean and standard deviation over the training window and normalizes test data accordingly.

name: Switch
desc: Selects from a variable number of slot inputs based on an integer index. Works on all data types. Use for regime-switching, multi-strategy routing, or conditional selection based on a classifier output.

name: Ultimate Oscillator
desc: Ultimate Oscillator. Multi-timeframe momentum oscillator that uses weighted average of three oscillators.

name: Maximum Sharpe Ratio

options.name: Lookback Period
options.desc: Number of periods for estimation
options.tuningGuidance: 252 (default, ~1 year daily). Max-Sharpe is highly sensitive to return estimates — longer lookbacks (504-756) produce more stable results. Short lookbacks (60-126) amplify estimation error and cause extreme weights.

options.name: Rebalance Frequency
options.desc: Number of periods between rebalancing (21 = monthly for daily data)
options.tuningGuidance: 21 (default, monthly). Max-Sharpe portfolios can have high turnover due to return estimate sensitivity. 63 (quarterly) reduces turnover. Pair with max_weight constraints to limit rebalancing churn.

options.name: Window Type
options.desc: Rolling (fixed-size sliding) or Expanding (cumulative)
options.tuningGuidance: rolling (default) adapts to recent return patterns. expanding reduces estimation noise by using all data — often preferred for max-Sharpe due to return estimation sensitivity.

options.name: Risk-Free Rate
options.desc: Annual risk-free rate
options.tuningGuidance: 0.0 (default). Set to current short-term rate (e.g., 0.05 for 5% fed funds). Affects which assets are attractive — higher risk-free rates shift weights away from low-return assets.

options.name: Annualization Factor
options.desc: Factor to annualize returns (252 for daily)
options.tuningGuidance: 252.0 (default for daily data). Use 52 for weekly data, 12 for monthly. Must match the frequency of the input returns for correct Sharpe ratio scaling.

options.name: Maximum Weight
options.desc: Maximum weight per asset
options.tuningGuidance: 1.0 (default) imposes no cap. Max-Sharpe is notorious for extreme concentration — setting 0.20-0.40 is strongly recommended. Without caps, the optimizer often puts 80%+ in a single asset.

desc: Maximum Sharpe Ratio portfolio (tangency portfolio) maximizes risk-adjusted returns. Optimizes (μ-rf)/σ where μ is expected return and σ is portfolio volatility.

name: Exponential Decay
desc: Exponential Decay. Applies exponential decay to each element in the input over the specified period.

name: Relative Strength Index

desc: Rate of Change. Measures percentage change between current price and price n periods ago.

name: Exponentially Weighted Moving Covariance

options.name: Span
options.desc: Span for exponential weighting (decay = 2/(1+span)). Higher values give more weight to history.
options.tuningGuidance: Use span=10-20 for fast-adapting risk models. Use span=30-60 for balanced adaptation. Use span=100+ for strategic risk analysis with smooth estimates. Roughly corresponds to rolling window of span/2 bars but with smoother transitions.

desc: Calculates covariance between two series using exponential weighting, emphasizing recent observations while smoothly incorporating history. Adapts faster than rolling covariance to changing relationships.

name: Ichimoku Kinko Hyo

options.name: Tenkan-sen Period
options.desc: Conversion line period: midpoint of highest high and lowest low
options.tuningGuidance: Standard 9 (represents 1.5 weeks in Japanese trading). Shorter periods for intraday, longer for weekly charts.

options.name: Kijun-sen Period
options.desc: Base line period and forward displacement for Senkou spans
options.tuningGuidance: Standard 26 (one month in Japanese trading). Also determines the forward shift for Senkou Span A/B and backward shift for Chikou.

options.name: Senkou Span B Period
options.desc: Period for Senkou Span B (slowest cloud boundary)
options.tuningGuidance: Standard 52 (two months). Longer periods create wider, more significant cloud zones. Shorter periods for faster markets.

desc: Ichimoku Kinko Hyo ('one glance equilibrium chart') - Japanese trend-following system providing five lines: Tenkan-sen (conversion), Kijun-sen (base), Senkou Span A/B (cloud), and Chikou Span (lagging). The cloud (Kumo) between Senkou A and B defines support/resistance zones and trend direction.

name: Average Directional Movement Index
desc: Average Directional Movement Index. Measures the strength of a trend, regardless of its direction.

name: ArgMin (Timestamp)

options.tuningGuidance: true (default) = expanding mode: at each row, returns the timestamp of the minimum value seen from the start up to that row. Useful for tracking when the current trough occurred. false = global mode: returns the same timestamp for every row — the date of the overall series minimum. Useful for labeling the worst day across an entire backtest.

desc: Returns the timestamp where the minimum value occurred. In expanding mode, tracks the running minimum's timestamp at each point. In global mode, broadcasts the single global argmin timestamp to all rows.

name: Klinger Volume Oscillator
desc: Klinger Volume Oscillator. Compares volume to price trends to identify reversals and divergence.

name: Retracements
desc: Calculates percentage retracements from swing highs and lows, measuring how much price has pulled back from a prior swing point.

name: Volume Weighted Moving Average
desc: Volume Weighted Moving Average. Moving average that weights price by volume, giving more importance to high-volume price moves.

name: Commodity Channel Index
desc: Commodity Channel Index. Identifies cyclical turns in price and measures variations from the statistical mean.

name: Linear Fit (Rolling OLS)

options.name: Window Size
options.desc: Rolling window size for OLS regression
options.tuningGuidance: Use 20-60 for tactical pairs trading. Use 60-120 for more stable hedge ratios. Match to expected holding period - shorter windows for intraday, longer for swing trading.

desc: Rolling ordinary least squares (OLS) regression. Fits y = slope*x + intercept over a rolling window. Returns slope, intercept, and residual (y - predicted) at each bar.

name: Break of Structure & Change of Character

options.desc: Use close price for break detection instead of high/low wicks
options.tuningGuidance: False (default) = wick-based breaks, more signals but some false. True = close-based breaks, more conservative but misses some valid breaks.

desc: Detects Break of Structure (BOS) and Change of Character (CHOCH) patterns, which signal potential trend changes and market structure shifts.

name: Dividends

name: Keltner Channels

options.name: Rolling Period
options.desc: Period for the EMA center line and ATR band width calculation
options.tuningGuidance: Standard 20 for daily charts. Use 10-15 for more responsive channels. Use 50 for long-term trend channels. Must match your trading timeframe.

options.name: Band Multiplier
options.desc: ATR multiplier for upper and lower band distance from center
options.tuningGuidance: Standard 2.0 ATR. Use 1.5 for tighter channels (more signals). Use 2.5-3.0 for wider channels (fewer but stronger breakout signals). In TTM Squeeze strategy, use 1.5 to compare with Bollinger Bands.

desc: ATR-based price channel developed by Chester Keltner (1960), modernized by Linda Raschke. Upper band = EMA + multiplier * ATR, Lower band = EMA - multiplier * ATR. Channel width adapts to volatility via ATR. Smoother than Bollinger Bands because ATR is less affected by individual outlier closes.

name: Keyword Count

options.name: Keywords
options.desc: List of keyword patterns to count in text. 'patterns': array of strings (plain substrings or regex). 'case_sensitive': false by default. 'use_regex': false by default. Each pattern's occurrences are counted independently and summed. Example: {patterns: ["risk", "uncertainty"], case_sensitive: false}

desc: Count total occurrences of all keyword patterns in text. Returns integer. More granular than keyword_match — returns intensity (how many?) not just presence (any?). Academic: Jegadeesh & Wu (2013) demonstrate term-weighting in 10-K filings predicts returns; keyness analysis via log-likelihood ratio identifies statistically significant term frequencies. Use for risk intensity scoring, keyword frequency analysis, measuring signal strength from text.

options.tuningGuidance: true (default) = expanding: at each row, tracks both min and max timestamps seen so far. false = global: broadcasts the overall min and max timestamps to all rows.

desc: Returns timestamps where both minimum and maximum values occurred. Outputs two columns: min_loc (timestamp of minimum) and max_loc (timestamp of maximum). More efficient than calling arg_min and arg_max separately when both are needed.

name: Datetime Extract

options.name: Datetime Component

Integer outputs: year (e.g. 2024), month (1-12), day (1-31), hour (0-23), minute (0-59), second (0-59), quarter (1-4), day_of_week (0=Mon..6=Sun ISO), day_of_year (1-366), week (1-53 ISO). Boolean output: is_leap_year. Timestamp output: date (truncated to midnight). Integer output: time_of_day (minutes since midnight).

options.name: Timezone
options.desc: IANA timezone for extraction (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London'). Timestamps are converted to this timezone before extraction. Critical for intraday: US DST shifts (Mar/Nov) create a 3-week gap with EU DST (last Sun Mar/Oct). Always convert before extracting hour/day components.

desc: Extract a datetime component (year, month, day, hour, etc.) from a timestamp. For bar timestamps, use datetime_extract(index()). For data source timestamps, pass them directly.

name: Positive Volume Index

Use cases include market sentiment analysis, short-squeeze prediction, risk management, and trading strategy refinement. Data is available across all plan tiers, updated bi-weekly with historical depth varying by subscription level (Basic: 2 years; Starter+: all history).

options.desc: Data source: CalendarSource.FRED for economic release dates, CalendarSource.Treasury for Treasury auction calendar

options.name: FRED Release ID
options.desc: FRED release ID for specific release schedule. Common IDs: 50=NFP, 10=CPI, 53=GDP, 46=Retail Sales, 101=FOMC. Set to 0 for all releases.

options.name: Treasury Security Type
options.desc: Treasury security type: TreasurySecurityType.Note, .Bond, or .Bill. Only used when source=CalendarSource.Treasury.

options.name: Treasury Term
options.desc: Treasury term filter (e.g., TreasuryTerm.Y10, TreasuryTerm.W4). Only used when source=CalendarSource.Treasury. Omit or leave empty for all terms.

name: Average Price
desc: Average Price. Calculates the average of open, high, low, and close prices.

name: Average Directional Movement Rating

name: Awesome Oscillator

name: XY Bars - ONE PER ASSET

options.name: Mode
options.desc: Mode: 'labeled' groups values by label column, 'series' creates one bar per value column via BarSeriesSchema
options.tuningGuidance: Use 'labeled' when you have a category column (month, sector). Use 'series' when each input column is a named bar.

options.name: Aggregation
options.desc: Aggregation function to apply to values
options.tuningGuidance: Required. Use Last for point-in-time, Mean for averages, Sum for totals.

options.name: Chart Title
options.desc: Title for the bar chart
options.tuningGuidance: Use a question-framed title hinting at the insight.

options.name: X Axis Label
options.desc: Label for the x-axis
options.tuningGuidance: Describe the categories.

options.name: Y Axis Label
options.desc: Label for the y-axis
options.tuningGuidance: Include units.

options.name: Category
options.desc: For grouping in dashboard
options.tuningGuidance: Required. Use numbered prefixes for ordering.

options.name: Vertical Bars
options.desc: Use vertical bars (column chart) or horizontal bars
options.tuningGuidance: Default true (vertical). Use horizontal for long category labels.

options.name: Stack Type
options.desc: NoStack (default), Normal (stacked), Percent (100% stacked). For grouped bars use BarSeriesSpec.stack to assign x-axis categories.
options.tuningGuidance: NoStack for comparison, Normal for composition, Percent for relative share.

options.name: Data Labels
options.desc: Show value labels on bars
options.tuningGuidance: Default true. Required by Exhibit A style guide for all bar charts.

options.name: Stack Labels
options.desc: Show totals on stacked bars
options.tuningGuidance: Enable when using stacked bars to show group totals.

options.name: Border Radius
options.desc: Bar corner radius (0-1, fraction of bar width)
options.tuningGuidance: Use 0 for sharp corners (default), 0.3-0.5 for rounded modern look.

options.name: Color By Value
options.desc: Color bars by value: positive=green (Success), negative=red (Error)
options.tuningGuidance: Enable for P&L or return charts where sign matters.

options.name: Y Axis Format

options.name: Y Axis Decimal Places

options.name: X Category Type
options.desc: How to interpret X labels: Exact (as-is), Month (1-12→Jan-Dec), DayOfWeek (1-7→Mon-Sun), Quarter (1-4→Q1-Q4), MonthYear (YYYYMM→Mon 'YY), QuarterYear (YYYYQ→QN 'YY), WeekYear (YYYYWW→WNN 'YY)
options.tuningGuidance: Use Month/DayOfWeek when labels are numeric calendar codes for automatic human-readable conversion.

options.name: Bar Width
options.desc: Fixed bar width in pixels (0 = auto)
options.tuningGuidance: Leave at 0 for auto-sizing. Set fixed width only for precise layout control.

options.name: Point Padding

options.tuningGuidance: Increase for more spacing, decrease for tighter bars.

options.name: Group Padding
options.desc: Space between groups of bars (0.0-1.0, -1 = default)
options.tuningGuidance: Increase for more separation between bar groups.

options.name: Y Plot Bands
options.desc: Horizontal shaded bands on Y axis (e.g., target zones, thresholds)
options.tuningGuidance: Add bands to highlight meaningful Y ranges.

options.name: X Plot Bands
options.desc: Vertical shaded bands on X axis (e.g., highlight categories)
options.tuningGuidance: Highlight specific category ranges.

options.name: Sort By Value
options.desc: Sort bars by aggregated value: None (default), Ascending (low→high), Descending (high→low)
options.tuningGuidance: Use Descending for rankings, None for natural category order.

options.name: Display Order
