options.name: Series Configuration
options.desc: Array of series specifications with name, color, and optional stack (x-axis category for grouped bars) for each input
options.tuningGuidance: Use in 'series' mode. Define one spec per input with name, color. Set stack field for grouped bar x-axis categories.

options.name: Overlay Line Series
options.desc: Line series overlaid on bars (e.g., moving averages). Each spec maps to one overlay input column.
options.tuningGuidance: Add trend lines or reference lines overlaid on bar data.

options.name: Reference Lines
options.desc: Horizontal/vertical threshold lines with optional labels, colors, and dash styles
options.tuningGuidance: Add zero line, averages, or thresholds for context.

desc: Categorical bar chart in the dashboard. Labeled mode: group values by label (months, sectors). Series mode: each column becomes a bar with BarSeriesSchema. Supports grouped, stacked, and 100%% stacked layouts.

name: Holiday Effect

options.name: Days Before Holiday
options.desc: Number of trading days before holiday

options.name: Days After Holiday
options.desc: Number of trading days after holiday

options.name: Holiday Calendar
options.desc: Holiday calendar to use for detecting holidays

options.name: Include Special Closes
options.desc: Include shortened session days (special closes) as holidays. When true, days with early closes are treated as holidays alongside fully closed days. Only applies to market calendars.

desc: Detects trading days before and after market holidays based on the pre-holiday effect documented by Lakonishok & Smidt (1988) and Ariel (1990). Research shows pre-holiday returns averaged 9-14 times the normal daily return during 1963-1982, with one-third of total annual stock market returns earned on just 8 pre-holiday trading days per year. The strongest effects occur before Independence Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas. The mechanism is attributed to reduced volume, lower selling pressure, short-covering before multi-day closures, and positive investor sentiment.

name: Inverse Volatility Weight

options.name: Maximum Weight
options.desc: Maximum weight per asset (caps individual weights, applied iteratively)
options.tuningGuidance: 1.0 (default) imposes no cap. Set to 0.25-0.40 for portfolios with 5+ assets to prevent concentration. Capping is applied iteratively — excess weight is redistributed to remaining assets.

options.name: Minimum Volatility
options.desc: Volatility floor to prevent low-vol assets from dominating. E.g., 0.05 means any asset with <5% vol is treated as having 5% vol. Set to 0 to disable.
options.tuningGuidance: 0.0 (default) disables the floor. Set to 0.01-0.05 when including money-market or very low-vol instruments that would otherwise absorb nearly all weight. Match roughly to the lowest reasonable annualized vol in the universe.

desc: Cross-sectional allocator that assigns weights inversely proportional to volatility. Higher volatility assets get lower weights. Formula: w_i = (1/vol_i) / sum(1/vol_j). Provides natural risk balancing without complex optimization. Use min_volatility to prevent very low-vol assets from dominating the portfolio.

name: Risk Parity

options.name: Lookback Period
options.desc: Number of periods for covariance estimation
options.tuningGuidance: 252 (default, ~1 year daily). Shorter (60-126) reacts faster to regime changes but noisier. Longer (504) for more stable estimates with slow-moving asset classes. Must exceed number of assets to ensure invertible covariance matrix.

options.name: Rebalance Frequency
options.desc: Number of periods between rebalancing (21 = monthly for daily data)
options.tuningGuidance: 21 (default, monthly). 5 (weekly) for tactical strategies with fast-moving correlations. 63 (quarterly) for lower turnover. Shorter step_size increases turnover and transaction costs.

options.name: Window Type
options.desc: Rolling (fixed-size sliding) or Expanding (cumulative)
options.tuningGuidance: rolling (default) adapts to recent conditions and forgets old data. expanding uses all available history — better for stable universes with long histories. Use rolling when regime changes matter.

options.name: Max Iterations
options.desc: Maximum iterations for Newton optimization
options.tuningGuidance: 1000 (default). Increase to 5000-10000 if convergence warnings appear with many assets (20+). Rarely needs adjustment for typical portfolios (3-15 assets).

options.name: Tolerance
options.desc: Convergence tolerance
options.tuningGuidance: 1e-8 (default). Tighten to 1e-10 for research requiring precise risk contribution equality. Loosen to 1e-6 for faster computation with many assets where approximate parity is sufficient.

options.name: Maximum Weight
options.desc: Maximum weight per asset (caps individual weights)
options.tuningGuidance: 1.0 (default) imposes no cap. Set to 0.25-0.40 for concentrated universes to prevent single-asset dominance. Tight caps may prevent exact risk parity — the optimizer finds the closest feasible solution.

desc: Equal Risk Contribution (ERC) portfolio where each asset contributes equally to total risk. Uses rolling estimation with configurable rebalance frequency. Uses Newton iteration to solve: RC_i = w_i * (Sigma*w)_i / port_vol = 1/N for all i. Reference: Maillard, Roncalli, Teiletche (2010).

name: Lowest Bars

options.name: Period
options.desc: Lookback period to search for lowest value
options.tuningGuidance: 260 for 52-week low, 20 for monthly low

desc: Returns how many bars ago the lowest value occurred within the lookback period. 0 means current bar is the low (new low / breakdown). Negative values indicate bars ago (-5 = low was 5 bars ago).

name: Hierarchical Equal Risk Contribution

options.name: Linkage Method
options.desc: Clustering linkage method: single, complete, average, ward
options.tuningGuidance: ward (default) produces balanced clusters with equal risk contribution. single produces chaining — less suitable for HERC. complete gives compact clusters. ward is strongly recommended for HERC to ensure meaningful cluster-level risk budgeting.

options.name: Lookback Period
options.desc: Number of periods for covariance estimation
options.tuningGuidance: 252 (default, ~1 year daily). Shorter (60-126) adapts faster but may produce unstable clusters. Longer (504) for more stable hierarchies. Must exceed number of assets.

options.name: Rebalance Frequency
options.desc: Number of periods between rebalancing (21 = monthly for daily data)
options.tuningGuidance: 21 (default, monthly). HERC has additional clustering overhead vs HRP. 63 (quarterly) reduces computation and turnover for stable universes.

options.name: Window Type
options.desc: Rolling (fixed-size sliding) or Expanding (cumulative)
options.tuningGuidance: rolling (default) adapts to recent correlation structure. expanding uses all available history — better when correlation structure is believed stable.

options.name: Max Clusters
options.desc: Maximum number of clusters to consider
options.tuningGuidance: 10 (default). Set to roughly sqrt(N) where N is the number of assets. For 5-10 assets use 3-5. For 50+ assets use 10-15. Too many clusters fragments the hierarchy; too few loses structure.

options.name: Risk Measure
options.desc: Risk measure: variance, vol
options.tuningGuidance: variance (default) penalizes large deviations quadratically — standard choice. vol (standard deviation) provides more intuitive risk units. Both produce similar allocations in practice.

options.name: Maximum Weight
options.desc: Maximum weight per asset (caps individual weights)
options.tuningGuidance: 1.0 (default) imposes no cap. HERC naturally diversifies within and across clusters, so caps are less critical. Set to 0.20-0.40 for large universes if needed.

desc: Hierarchical Equal Risk Contribution extends HRP by finding optimal clusters and ensuring equal risk contribution between clusters. Allocates inter-cluster by inverse risk and intra-cluster by inverse variance. Reference: Riskfolio-Lib.

name: Minimum Variance

options.name: Lookback Period
options.desc: Number of periods for covariance estimation
options.tuningGuidance: 252 (default, ~1 year daily). Shorter (60-126) adapts faster but covariance estimates are noisier and may produce unstable weights. Longer (504) for more stable portfolios. Must exceed number of assets for invertible covariance.

options.name: Rebalance Frequency
options.desc: Number of periods between rebalancing (21 = monthly for daily data)
options.tuningGuidance: 21 (default, monthly). Min-variance weights can shift significantly between rebalances when correlations change. 5 (weekly) for fast adaptation. 63 (quarterly) for lower turnover at the cost of slower adaptation.

options.name: Window Type
options.desc: Rolling (fixed-size sliding) or Expanding (cumulative)
options.tuningGuidance: rolling (default) adapts to recent volatility regimes. expanding uses all available history — produces smoother weights but slower to adapt to new regimes.

options.name: Maximum Weight
options.desc: Maximum weight per asset
options.tuningGuidance: 1.0 (default) imposes no cap. Min-variance often concentrates heavily in low-vol assets — setting 0.20-0.40 is common to enforce diversification. Essential for universes with a clear low-vol outlier.

desc: Minimum Variance portfolio minimizes total portfolio volatility. Uses rolling estimation with configurable rebalance frequency. Finds weights that minimize w'Σw subject to sum(w)=1, w>=0. Does not require expected return estimates.

name: Minimum CVaR

options.name: Lookback Period
options.desc: Number of periods for estimation
options.tuningGuidance: 252 (default, ~1 year daily). CVaR estimation needs sufficient tail observations — shorter lookbacks (< 126) may lack enough extreme events. 504-756 recommended for reliable tail estimates. More data is especially important at low alpha.

options.name: Rebalance Frequency
options.desc: Number of periods between rebalancing (21 = monthly for daily data)
options.tuningGuidance: 21 (default, monthly). CVaR-optimal weights shift with tail risk changes. 63 (quarterly) for lower turnover. Weekly rebalancing rarely justified given tail estimation noise.

options.name: Window Type
options.desc: Rolling (fixed-size sliding) or Expanding (cumulative)
options.tuningGuidance: rolling (default) adapts to recent tail behavior. expanding uses all data — often preferred for CVaR since tail events are rare and more data improves tail estimates.

options.name: Confidence Level
options.desc: CVaR confidence level (e.g., 0.05 = 5% worst cases)
options.tuningGuidance: 0.05 (default, 5% tail). Lower values (0.01-0.025) focus on more extreme tails but require much more data. Higher values (0.10-0.20) smooth the estimate by averaging over more scenarios. 0.05 is the industry standard.

options.name: Maximum Weight
options.desc: Maximum weight per asset
options.tuningGuidance: 1.0 (default) imposes no cap. CVaR optimization can concentrate in assets with thin tails. Set to 0.20-0.40 to enforce diversification, especially with fat-tailed assets.

desc: Minimum CVaR (Conditional Value at Risk, Expected Shortfall) portfolio minimizes expected loss in the worst α% of scenarios. Better captures tail risk than variance.

name: Black-Litterman

options.name: Lookback Period
options.desc: Number of periods for covariance estimation
options.tuningGuidance: 252 (default, ~1 year daily). Longer lookbacks (504-756) improve equilibrium return estimates. Shorter (126) adapts faster but adds noise to the Bayesian blend. Must exceed number of assets.

options.name: Rebalance Frequency
options.desc: Number of periods between rebalancing (21 = monthly for daily data)
options.tuningGuidance: 21 (default, monthly). BL weights are typically more stable than raw mean-variance due to the shrinkage effect. 63 (quarterly) is common in practice.

options.name: Window Type
options.desc: Rolling (fixed-size sliding) or Expanding (cumulative)
options.tuningGuidance: rolling (default) adapts to recent conditions. expanding leverages all data for the equilibrium estimate — often preferred for BL since the model already regularizes via the prior.

options.name: Prior Uncertainty
options.desc: Uncertainty scalar for prior (typically 0.025-0.05)
options.tuningGuidance: 0.05 (default). Lower values (0.01-0.025) give more weight to the equilibrium prior — more conservative, closer to market-cap weighting. Higher values (0.1-0.5) give more weight to historical returns — more aggressive, closer to sample mean-variance.

options.name: Risk Aversion
options.desc: Market risk aversion coefficient
options.tuningGuidance: 2.5 (default, standard market estimate). Higher values (3-5) imply the market demands more return per unit risk — equilibrium returns are higher. Lower values (1-2) assume less risk aversion. Derived from market Sharpe ratio and volatility.

options.name: Annualization Factor
options.desc: Factor to annualize returns
options.tuningGuidance: 252.0 (default for daily data). Use 52 for weekly data, 12 for monthly. Must match input return frequency for correct equilibrium return calculation.

options.name: Maximum Weight
options.desc: Maximum weight per asset
options.tuningGuidance: 1.0 (default) imposes no cap. BL produces more stable weights than raw mean-variance, but caps of 0.25-0.50 are still recommended for concentrated universes.

desc: Black-Litterman model combines market equilibrium with investor views using Bayesian inference. This simplified version blends equilibrium returns with historical returns for more stable estimates.

name: Minimum Semivariance

options.name: Lookback Period
options.desc: Number of periods for estimation
options.tuningGuidance: 252 (default, ~1 year daily). Semivariance uses only below-benchmark observations, so effective sample size is roughly half. Longer lookbacks (504) improve stability. Must exceed number of assets.

options.name: Rebalance Frequency
options.desc: Number of periods between rebalancing (21 = monthly for daily data)
options.tuningGuidance: 21 (default, monthly). 63 (quarterly) for lower turnover. Semivariance estimates are noisier than full variance, so less frequent rebalancing may reduce whipsaw.

options.name: Window Type
options.desc: Rolling (fixed-size sliding) or Expanding (cumulative)
options.tuningGuidance: rolling (default) adapts to recent downside patterns. expanding uses all data — often preferred since downside observations are scarcer and more data improves semicovariance estimates.

options.name: Benchmark Return
options.desc: Benchmark return for downside calculation (typically 0)
options.tuningGuidance: 0.0 (default) treats any negative return as downside. Set to the risk-free daily rate (e.g., 0.0002 for ~5% annual) to measure downside relative to a hurdle. Positive values raise the bar for what counts as downside.

options.name: Maximum Weight
options.desc: Maximum weight per asset
options.tuningGuidance: 1.0 (default) imposes no cap. Like min-variance, semivariance optimization can concentrate in low-downside assets. Set to 0.20-0.40 for diversified portfolios.

desc: Minimum Semivariance portfolio minimizes downside risk only, ignoring upside volatility. Uses semicovariance matrix computed from returns below the benchmark.

name: Donchian Channel

options.name: Window Size
options.desc: Lookback period for highest high and lowest low
options.tuningGuidance: Classic Turtle Trading uses 20 for entry, 10 for exit. Shorter periods (10-15) for more responsive but noisier breakout signals. Longer periods (50-55) for capturing larger trend moves.

desc: Price channel formed by the highest high and lowest low over a rolling window, with a middle line at the average. Used in the famous Turtle Trading system. Breakout above the upper channel signals potential uptrend; below the lower channel signals potential downtrend.

name: Trade Count
desc: Number of trades per bar (provider 'n').

name: Price Distance
desc: Measures the normalized price distance using OHLC data. Computes a composite distance metric from open, high, low, and close prices, useful for detecting unusual price movement patterns and market activity levels.

name: Market Facilitation Index
desc: Market Facilitation Index. Measures market readiness to move prices with minimal volume.

name: Aroon Oscillator
desc: Aroon Oscillator. Subtracts Aroon Down from Aroon Up, measuring the strength of a prevailing trend.

name: Elder's Market Thermometer

options.name: Period
options.desc: EMA period for smoothing the thermometer reading
options.tuningGuidance: Standard 22 (approximately one month). Shorter periods for more responsive readings. Longer for smoother trend assessment.

options.name: Buy Factor
options.desc: Multiplier for generating buy signals relative to the EMA
options.tuningGuidance: Default 0.1. Lower values generate fewer but more selective buy signals.

options.name: Sell Factor
options.desc: Multiplier for generating sell signals relative to the EMA
options.tuningGuidance: Default 0.5. Higher values require more extreme readings for sell signals.

desc: Elder's Market Thermometer measures the true range activity of the market and compares it to an EMA for signal generation. Developed by Alexander Elder. Outputs the raw thermometer reading, its EMA, and buy/sell signals based on configurable factors relative to the smoothed reading.

name: Forward Returns

options.name: Period
options.desc: Number of periods to look forward
options.tuningGuidance: Period 1 for next bar returns. Larger periods for longer-term forward returns. Common: 1 (next bar), 5 (next week on daily), 20 (next month). Use as target variable for machine learning predictions.

options.name: Return Type
options.desc: Type of return calculation
options.tuningGuidance: Simple returns: (future_price - price) / price. Log returns: log(future_price / price). Log returns are more symmetric and better for ML models. Simple returns are more intuitive for interpretation.

desc: Calculates future returns by looking ahead N periods. For each bar, computes the return from current price to future price. Essential for creating target variables in predictive models.

name: Ease of Movement
desc: Ease of Movement. Relates price change to volume, identifying whether price changes are easy or difficult.

name: Variable Index Dynamic Average
desc: Variable Index Dynamic Average. Adapts to volatility by modifying the smoothing constant used in calculations.

name: Bollinger Bands %B
desc: Measures position within Bollinger Bands as a normalized value between 0 and 1. Values above 1 or below 0 indicate extreme conditions.

name: Bar Gap

options.name: Fill Percentage
options.desc: Minimum fill percentage for gap_filled signal
options.tuningGuidance: 100% for complete fill. Lower values for partial fill detection.

options.name: Minimum Gap Size
options.desc: Minimum gap size as percentage to detect. Gaps smaller than this are ignored. Example: 0.04 for 4-pip gaps on EUR/USD.
options.tuningGuidance: Set above typical bid-ask spread to filter noise.

desc: Detects price gaps between any consecutive bars (liquidity gaps, fair value gaps, trading halt gaps) and tracks whether price retraces to fill them. No session boundary requirement.

name: Cross-Sectional First/Last

options.name: Group By
options.desc: Group assets before applying cross-sectional operation. When set, the transform operates within each group independently.
options.tuningGuidance: Use 'sector' for industry-neutral stock strategies. Use 'category' for futures. Use 'auto_detect' to let the system choose.

desc: Returns the first and last non-null values across assets at each timestamp as a two-element tuple. Order is determined by the asset/column position in the DataFrame. Outputs: (first_value, last_value).

name: Mean Deviation Over Period
desc: Mean Deviation Over Period. Calculates the mean deviation over the specified period.

name: Intraday Returns

options.name: Return Type
options.desc: Type of return calculation
options.tuningGuidance: Simple returns: (close - open) / open. Log returns: log(close / open).

desc: Calculates the return from open to close within each bar. Measures intraday price movement.

name: Cross-Sectional Labeled Lines - ONE FOR ALL ASSETS

options.name: Chart Title
options.desc: Title for the line chart
options.tuningGuidance: Use comparative title (e.g., 'Yield Curve by Country').

options.name: X Axis Label
options.desc: Label for the x-axis
options.tuningGuidance: Describe the category dimension (e.g., 'Tenor').

options.name: Y Axis Label
options.desc: Label for the y-axis
options.tuningGuidance: Include units.

options.name: Category
options.desc: Category for grouping in dashboard
options.tuningGuidance: Required.

options.name: X Axis Labels
options.desc: Category labels for the X axis. Number of labels must match the number of NumericTuple inputs per asset.
options.tuningGuidance: Define the categorical X axis points (e.g., ['1M', '3M', '6M', '1Y', '2Y', '5Y', '10Y', '30Y']).

options.name: Y Reference Lines
options.desc: Horizontal reference lines on Y axis with optional labels, colors, and dash styles
options.tuningGuidance: Add zero line or benchmark levels.

options.name: Y Axis Format
options.desc: Format type for Y axis values (Auto, Decimal, Percent, Monetary, Integer)
options.tuningGuidance: Use PercentFormat for yields/rates.

options.name: Y Axis Decimal Places
options.desc: Number of decimal places for Y axis values
options.tuningGuidance: Default 2.

options.name: Aggregation
options.desc: Aggregation function for each asset's values per x_label (Last, Mean, Median, etc.)
options.tuningGuidance: Default Last. Use Mean for averaged profiles.

options.name: Smooth Lines
options.desc: Whether to smooth the lines (spline interpolation)
options.tuningGuidance: Enable for term structure visualization.

options.name: Data Labels
options.desc: Show value labels on data points (default: true)
options.tuningGuidance: Default true. Disable if many assets make labels overlap.

options.name: Line Colors
options.desc: Per-asset line colors (e.g., Blue, Red, Success)
options.tuningGuidance: Assign distinct colors per asset. Blue primary.

options.name: Asset Filters
options.desc: Filter which assets to display based on ranking criteria. Each filter specifies: rank ('top'/'bottom'), count (number of assets), column (metric to rank by). Chain multiple filters with op ('AND'/'OR').
options.tuningGuidance: Use to focus on a subset.

options.name: Maximum Assets
options.desc: Maximum number of assets to display (0 = no limit). Applied after filters.
options.tuningGuidance: Reduce for readability.

options.name: Display Order
options.desc: Display order within dashboard category (lower values appear first, 0 = default position)

desc: Cross-sectional line chart with categorical X axis where each asset becomes a named line. Use for comparing yield curves, factor profiles, or term structures across multiple assets — each asset traces its own curve across the same category labels.

name: Turn of Month

options.name: Days Before Month End
options.desc: Number of trading days before month end to include
options.tuningGuidance: Research suggests 1-2 days before month end. More days may dilute effect.

options.name: Days After Month Start
options.desc: Number of trading days after month start to include
options.tuningGuidance: Research suggests 3-4 days after month start. Test on your specific market.

desc: Detects the turn-of-month calendar anomaly documented by Ariel (1987) and Lakonishok & Smidt (1988). Marks the last N trading days of the month and the first M trading days of the next month. The original research found that all positive DJIA returns over 90 years (1897-1986) occurred within the 4-day window from day -1 to day +3. The effect is attributed to pension fund flows, payroll timing (401k contributions), and institutional rebalancing at month boundaries. Returns during the TOM window average 5-12 basis points per day higher than non-TOM days.

outputs.name: Turn of Month Active (True during TOM window)

name: Price Profile

options.name: Window Size
options.desc: Number of bars for volume profile calculation
options.tuningGuidance: Smaller windows (10-20) for intraday. Larger (50-100) for swing trading.

options.name: Tick Size
options.desc: Price bin granularity
options.tuningGuidance: Match to asset tick size. Smaller = more detail but slower.

options.name: Value Area %
options.desc: Percentage of volume for Value Area (standard is 70%)
options.tuningGuidance: 70% is standard (1 std dev). Use 80% for wider zones, 60% for tighter.

options.name: Profile Mode
options.desc: volume=Volume Profile (volume at price), market=Market Profile (Time Price Opportunity)
options.tuningGuidance: Volume mode aggregates actual volume. TPO mode counts bar touches per level.

options.name: Initial Balance Periods
options.desc: Number of bars for Initial Balance calculation (0=disabled)
options.tuningGuidance: For intraday, use 2 for first hour IB (30min bars). 0 disables IB output.

desc: Rolling Volume/Market Profile analysis. Volume mode computes POC and Value Area based on traded volume. TPO mode (Market Profile) counts time spent at each price level. Optional Initial Balance tracks the range of the first N bars.

outputs.name: Point of Control - price with highest activity

name: SuperTrend

options.name: ATR Period
options.desc: Period for Average True Range calculation
options.tuningGuidance: Shorter periods (7-10) for faster signals. Longer (14-21) for smoother trends.

options.name: Multiplier
options.desc: ATR multiplier for band width
options.tuningGuidance: Higher multiplier (3-4) = fewer signals, stronger trends. Lower (1.5-2) = more responsive but more false signals.

desc: Trend-following indicator using ATR-based bands. Flips between upper and lower band based on price breakouts. Provides clear trend direction and trailing stop levels.

name: Optimal f

options.name: Minimum Trades
options.desc: Minimum trades required before using Optimal f
options.tuningGuidance: 30 (default). Optimal f is more sensitive to small samples than Kelly because it uses the full return distribution and normalizes by worst loss. 50+ recommended for strategies with variable returns.

options.name: Fallback Percent
options.desc: Equity percentage to use when insufficient trade history (10 = 10%)
options.tuningGuidance: 10.0 (default). Same guidance as kelly.fallback_pct — should roughly match expected optimal f allocation to avoid discontinuity at switchover.

options.name: Maximum Leverage
